title: Black Hole Recordings New Releases – Week 47
excerpt: Find the latest electronic music news, features, interviews, videos and podcasts from Beatportal - the reference for DJs and dance music artists.
content:
A selection of this week’s standout releases across the dancefloor.

This week, a trance favourite gets a modern rework, while a spontaneous studio session leads to a new release and a festival anthem draws inspiration from singing under the moon. There’s also a tribute to the sounds of trance’s golden era, another addition to the Airscape catalogue, and melodic techno built around the feeling of losing yourself in music.

Plastic Boy - Silver Bath (Fish56Octagon Remix) [Black Hole Recordings]

Fish56Octagon’s connection to this release goes beyond putting a new spin on a beloved record. Known for his deep knowledge of dance music and his love of records from the ’90s and early 2000s, he has built a following by sharing the tracks and sounds that shaped his musical taste. He also made his production debut with a rework of Man With No Name’s trance classic “Floor Essence,” alongside David Forbes, showing his interest in giving much-loved records a new life.

Fish6Octagon first heard Plastic Boy’s “Silver Bath” at The Gallery in London, where the track’s dramatic bassline and key change left a lasting impression. A fan of M.I.K.E. Push’s productions from that era, he wanted to bring the 2002 classic into his own DJ sets, creating a version that stays close to the original while updating the drums and bass and adding an acid line.

I was blown away and honoured to have the opportunity to be included in that. It’s very special to be involved.

- Fish56Octagon

The Quest - Afterlife [In Trance We Trust]

The idea behind “Afterlife” came from a rather ordinary evening. On September 9, Benno de Goeij decided to put Netflix aside and spend some time in the studio instead. With no particular plan or expectations, he simply followed whatever came to mind, letting the music develop naturally. The result was a snapshot of his creative mind on an average evening, when he can make music without thinking about trends, outside influences, or what others might expect.

Released on In Trance We Trust, “Afterlife” captures that spontaneous moment of inspiration, pairing Benno’s natural creative flow with an unmistakable old-school trance sound that recalls the era when the genre first captured his imagination. It offers a glimpse into his world and the music that comes naturally when he is simply doing what he loves.

Frankyeffe x Brittany Egbert - Cry to the Moon [Magik Muzik]

“Cry to the Moon” takes its title quite literally, building around the image of a festival crowd singing together under the night sky. Frankyeffe’s uplifting trance production gives Brittany Egbert’s songwriting a setting that feels made for those late-night festival moments, with harmonies designed to be sung back by the crowd rather than just listened to.

Inspired by the image of people raising their voices together like wolves howling at the moon, the song carries a sense of shared emotion and connection. Fittingly, Frankyeffe and Brittany will debut it together at Dreamstate SoCal on release day – the perfect embodiment of the festival for dreamers.

Storm x Alt1 – Storm [Black Hole Recordings]

Storm x Alt1 revisits one of trance’s most recognisable melodies, originally released in 1998 by Jam El Mar and Mark Spoon, better known as Jam & Spoon. For Alt1, aka Sneijder, the record is more than just a classic to rework. Their music has been a major influence on his own journey, making this release a chance to pay tribute to the sounds that shaped him as a DJ and producer. While the new version brings the original into a modern setting, it retains the melody that made it so memorable.

It’s an honour to team up and put my stamp on such a legendary record. The melody is simple but effective, and it takes me right back to my youth and the days when I was learning my craft as a DJ on vinyl.

– Alt1

Johan Gielen presents Airscape – Meraki [Black Hole Recordings]

Johan Gielen continues to explore the sound that has made Airscape such a beloved project, and “Meraki” is another beautiful addition to the catalogue. “Made From Within” perfectly captures the spirit of the release, as the track comes from Johan’s love for trance and the emotions that come with it. Combining energy and emotion, it feels like a personal expression of everything the genre means to him, created without following trends or boundaries, but simply from the love of a sound that has always been part of him.

Ina Sapphire - Hit That [Force Of Habit]

“Hit That” captures the feeling of getting completely lost in music, where the outside world slowly fades away and all that matters is the rhythm. Ina Sapphire builds the track around a driving melodic techno beat, layering atmospheric synths and emotional melodies that gradually take over the record. As the tension builds, the production becomes more powerful, balancing its energetic groove with a melodic touch that gives it character. Inspired by those moments when you stop thinking and simply feel the music, “Hit That” is an invitation to let go and get carried away by the sound.
